# Atmospheric Alerts Computer The atmospheric alerts computer displays information about every air alarm and fire alarm on the station.
It is a useful tool for quickly finding areas that require attention.
The atmospheric alerts computer is often located in Atmospherics, where atmospheric technicians use it to monitor conditions throughout the station. However, it also gives other engineers a good indication of where the station has been damaged.
The computer lists air alarms in the [color=orange]Warning[/color] and [color=red]Danger[/color] states. It also displays the location of every air alarm on a map, color-coded according to its current status.
Air alarms with a Normal status are hidden by default. Their visibility can be toggled with the filters at the bottom of the interface.
The map draws an outline around the area monitored by each air alarm, helping you locate dangerous zones. The color of this outline changes according to the alarm's status.
If an air alarm has no power, it appears gray in both the list and the map.
Clicking an air alarm in the list or on the map displays detailed information about the atmosphere in that area, helping you identify the type of emergency in progress.
The atmospheric alerts computer also displays a list of triggered [textlink="fire alarms" link="FireAndGasControl"] on a separate tab. This lets you quickly locate areas where a fire may be burning.
Individual alerts, such as those from combustion chambers and freezers, can be silenced: select the alert in the list and press the "Silence alerts" button. This hides the alert from the list, but it remains visible on the map.
